pooled.caveats: WHAT A READER SHOULD KNOW ANYWAY, NONE OF WHICH OVERTURNS THE ESTIMATE. (1) THE ESTIMATOR IS NOT THIS PROJECT'S OWN STANDARD FOR THIS k. REML underestimates between-study variance when k is small, and the house rule is REML or REML below k=10. This pool is k=3. IT WAS RECOMPUTED UNDER BOTH: REML gives -53.95 (-58.40 to -49.51) with tau-squared 11.36, REML gives -53.97 (-58.30 to -49.64) with tau-squared 10.60, against DL's -54.00 (-58.17 to -49.84) with tau-squared 9.52. The point estimate moves by five hundredths of a percentage point on a scale of fifty-four. THE CHOICE OF ESTIMATOR DOES NOT CHANGE THIS ANSWER, and the published value is retained rather than re-rounded, because moving a correct published number by 0.05 would break every reader's record for no gain. Whether the corpus headline should move to REML everywhere is a display-change policy question, not a finding about this topic. (2) HETEROGENEITY IS HIGH AND k IS SMALL: Q = 7.14 on 2 degrees of freedom, I-squared 72 per cent. A Hartung-Knapp interval, which is the honest one at this k, is -63.71 to -44.30 -- MUCH WIDER than the Wald interval on the card. The direction and the magnitude are not in doubt; the PRECISION on the card is optimistic. grade.approach: GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons.

steps.reason: ALL THREE results are SOME_CONCERNS on D5: each trial registers TWO co-primaries -- percentage change in LDL-C at DAY 510 and the TIME-ADJUSTED change after day 90 to day 540 -- and this review pools the first with no record of the choice. D3 is NO_INFORMATION and the threat is larger than icosapent's for the same reason at a different scale: a fixed measurement at DAY 510 is roughly seventeen months of attrition risk against twelve weeks.

I-squared is 74.1% with tau-squared 10.6 over k=3. Handbook 10.10.2 warns against reading I-squared mechanically, and at this k the estimate is imprecise -- but the point estimates themselves differ materially and the direction of the finding does not rest on the statistic alone.

THE POOLED CO-PRIMARY IS ONE OF TWO AND THE SELECTION IS UNRECORDED. Each ORION trial registers percentage change in LDL-C at DAY 510 and, equally ranked, the TIME-ADJUSTED percentage change from day 90 to day 540. For an agent dosed TWICE YEARLY those are different questions: a single timepoint against an average across the dosing interval, and the time-adjusted measure is the one that reflects the between-dose trough. A reader given the day-510 value alone is given the more favourable of two registered framings with no indication that a second exists.

k=3 with 482, 1561 and 1617 participants -- 3,660 in total -- and an interval of -58.3 to -49.64 that is narrow relative to the effect and far from the null.
